name: Turkmenistan
summary_text: Turkmenistan is a place trans visitors should avoid entirely. Male same-sex conduct is criminalised (up to 2 years under Article 135) and, more fundamentally, Turkmenistan is one of the world's most closed states: the state exerts strict media control and heavy internet monitoring, no independent research on LGBTI issues has been possible since 2019, and asylum is the community's most urgent need (ILGA-Europe). Amnesty has documented systematic abuses. There is no legal gender recognition, no community, no recourse, and no visibility — the only safe strategy is total concealment. For a visitor: any discoverable online presence or visible nonconformity is dangerous in a state that monitors communications pervasively.

sources.claim_summary: ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2025 (covering 2024) chapter on Turkmenistan: asylum remains one of the most urgent needs for the LGBTI community; the only documented research on LGBTI issues dates to 2019 (data collection almost impossible due to safety risks); Amnesty documented systemic discrimination; the April 2022 Criminal Code kept 'sodomy' provisions and increased the severity and scope of punishments; torture and inhumane treatment by law enforcement reported, with several LGBTI people forced to flee; the Ministry of National Security collaborates with regional AIDS centres, exposing HIV-test data.

sources.title: Turkmenistan - United States Department of State
sources.claim_summary: US State Department 2021 Human Rights Report for Turkmenistan: official assessment - same-sex conduct criminalised under Article 135 (up to 2 years); societal stigma; the totalitarian state's pervasive repression.

EHPV (Estonian Network of People Living with HIV) mid-term UPR submission (2020) on Turkmenistan: LGBT persons and PLHIV 'have no effective legislative means of enjoying their fundamental human rights'; Article 135 criminalises consensual same-sex acts; LGBT persons are increasingly fleeing to the EU to seek refuge.

ECOM Legal Environment Assessment (2019, with Turkmen.news): legislative analysis related to LGBT rights and HIV in Turkmenistan - identifies legal barriers for PLHIV, gay men, MSM and trans people, analysing law-enforcement practice and international recommendations.
Columbia Law School (May 2007): the Sexuality and Gender Law Clinic secured asylum for a Turkmen woman who feared persecution because she is a lesbian in the mostly Muslim country.

Goldberg Kohn (Sept 2019): attorneys secured asylum for a lesbian couple from Turkmenistan who feared persecution including imprisonment and torture; homosexuality is punishable by up to 2 years; suspects face interrogation, torture and confinement to mental hospitals; women are vulnerable to sexual violence and 'honor killings'.
